summary_paragraph: Mrs. ___ was admitted for acute asthma exacerbation with progressive shortness of breath, cough, and wheezing. Despite initial treatment with steroids and bronchodilators, she showed limited improvement and developed radiographic evidence of right upper lobe pneumonia, prompting initiation of IV ceftriaxone and continuation of levofloxacin. She experienced transient gastrointestinal symptoms, which resolved without specific treatment, and right-sided chest pain attributed to pleuritic irritation from pneumonia rather than cardiac ischemia, as confirmed by ECG and cardiology review. Her hypertension was managed throughout, and she was discharged on a prednisone taper, antibiotics, adjusted lisinopril dosing, and new allergy medication. Smoking cessation was strongly advised given her respiratory decline, and she expressed willingness to quit. She improved clinically, with stable oxygenation and reduced work of breathing, and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up instructions.
